rules.threshold_text: 75 MW or more at a single site (16 TAC §25.194); Batch Zero applies primarily to large electric loads of 75 MW or greater (AEP)
rules.contract_term: a standard large load interconnection agreement (SLLIA) once ERCOT allocates capacity, binding the customer to the minimum billing demand for the period set in §25.193; no term printed in §25.194 or AEP's 10-Q
rules.collateral: 16 TAC §25.194: $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand at the intermediate agreement; the greater of $50,000 per MW of contracted peak demand or allocated system upgrade costs at the SLLIA; cash collateral held in a segregated interest-bearing account; direct interconnection costs as cash CIAC; AEP Texas segregated about $1.2 billion of cash collateral in October 2026 and received about $2 billion of Batch Zero security in July 2026 as cash, corporate or parental guarantees and letters of credit; the accepted forms besides cash collateral are a guaranty (guarantor rated at least BBB- or Baa3) or a letter of credit from a major bank rated at least A- or A3
rules.exit_fee: 16 TAC §25.194: 20% of the security for allocated capacity kept on withdrawal before the SLLIA deadline, 20% of the security for withdrawn contracted demand kept after a SLLIA, a customer that neither withdraws before the SLLIA deadline nor executes a SLLIA forfeits the security posted under its intermediate agreement; CIAC not refundable (statewide row)
rules.study_timeline: 16 TAC §25.194: $100,000 study fee; the TSP or DSP contacts ERCOT within 60 days after the intermediate agreement is executed and funded and tells the customer within five working days; AEP's 10-Q reports ERCOT's Batch Zero study paused (notes)

rules.threshold_text: no MW threshold for full cost recovery (it applies to all customers, large loads included); Austin Energy's local study, cost and obligation requirements are presented for large customer requests under 75 MW; the repealed Code Section 15-9-5 applied to loads over four megawatts
rules.collateral: the customer pays 100 percent of infrastructure costs (CIAC, exemption for certified affordable housing); the former 50 percent deposit or bond for loads over 4 MW is repealed; Austin Energy keeps its authority to assess a deposit or other security as necessary (no amount printed)

rules.utility: Bryan Texas Utilities (BTU), City of Bryan
rules.threshold_text: peak demand of 10 MW or more and less than 75 MW, at transmission voltage, customer procuring its own power supply (General Service Transmission, bundled, applies up to 75 MW)

75 MW or more at a single site (16 TAC §25.194, as for every ERCOT TSP and DSP; Oncor's 10-Q gives the same 75 MW for ERCOT's batch framework); in Oncor's tariff a load too large to be served economically or practically at primary or secondary voltage, as Oncor determines, takes transmission voltage service
rules.contract_term: tariff form: the Transmission/Substation Facility Extension Agreement takes effect on execution, with no minimum term; the customer may terminate before the Company Facilities are complete on seven days' written notice; under 16 TAC §25.194 the SLLIA binds the customer to the minimum billing demand for the period set in §25.193
rules.collateral: 16 TAC §25.194: $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand at the intermediate agreement, then the greater of $50,000 per MW of contracted peak demand or the allocated system upgrade costs at the SLLIA, and direct interconnection costs as cash CIAC (full terms in the statewide row); Oncor's tariff form: Oncor may require a security payment in advance of construction to cover the costs owed if the customer's facilities do not reach the specified level of operation by the specified date; Batch Zero: $50,000 per MW requested, cash deposits converted within a specified number of days into letters of credit or approved affiliate guarantees; customers below Oncor's credit quality thresholds post security before construction
rules.exit_fee: tariff form: on termination before completion the customer pays Oncor's costs incurred, its committed costs it cannot avoid and the cost of restoring the system, less the customer's payments; if the customer's facilities miss the specified level of operation by the specified date, the customer pays the costs the agreement specifies; 16 TAC §25.194: 20% of the security for allocated or contracted capacity kept on withdrawal, security forfeited if no SLLIA is signed, CIAC not refundable (statewide row)
rules.study_timeline: 16 TAC §25.194: $100,000 study fee at the intermediate agreement; Oncor, as interconnecting TSP or DSP, must contact ERCOT to start the study within 60 days after the intermediate agreement is executed and funded and tell the customer within five working days; no Oncor-specific study duration in its tariff or SEC filings

rules.utility: Texas TSPs and DSPs in ERCOT (PUCT rule)
rules.threshold_text: 75 MW: a large load customer not energized by 8 October 2026 that seeks a new interconnection at a single site of 75 MW or more, an expansion reaching 75 MW for the first time, an expansion of a site over 75 MW by 75 MW or more, or co-location with a generation resource; at transmission or distribution voltage; for an expansion the rule applies to the added load
rules.contract_term: no term printed in §25.194: an intermediate agreement before the study, then a commission-approved pro forma SLLIA (to be adopted in a future rulemaking) whose minimum billing obligation runs for the period set in §25.193
rules.collateral: intermediate agreement: $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand (or of the incremental increase), posted at execution; SLLIA: the greater of $50,000 per MW of contracted peak demand or the system upgrade costs allocated by the (batch zero) interconnection study, posted at SLLIA execution, plus possible additional security for the minimum billing demand; accepted forms: cash in a segregated interest-bearing account, a guaranty from a guarantor rated at least BBB- (S&P), Baa3 (Moody's) or BBB- (Fitch), or a letter of credit from a bank rated at least A-, A3 or A-; the $50,000 adjusted by CPI every five years from 2032; direct interconnection costs paid as non-refundable cash CIAC with no allowance
rules.exit_fee: outstanding amounts owed are paid first (costs incurred, non-cancellable equipment, construction and services, and after a SLLIA the minimum billing demand for its set period); withdrawal before the study, or after a zero-MW allocation: full return of the rest; withdrawal after a partial allocation but before the SLLIA deadline: 20% of the security for the allocated capacity kept (50% for batch zero loads under Planning Guide 9.2.1.1(1)(f)); no SLLIA by the deadline: security forfeited; withdrawal of contracted demand after a SLLIA: 20% of the security for the withdrawn demand kept; energization schedule missed by 24 months: security drawn for amounts owed and 20% of the security for the non-utilized capacity kept; CIAC not refundable
rules.study_timeline: $100,000 study fee due at execution of the intermediate agreement (ERCOT may add a flat fee); the TSP or DSP must contact ERCOT to start the study within 60 days after the intermediate agreement is executed and funded, and tell the customer within five working days; unused study fee returned within 60 days after the study ends

rules.utility: Tri-County Electric Cooperative, Inc. (Azle, Texas; a Brazos Electric Power Cooperative member)
rules.threshold_text: 2 MW: "two megawatts or greater" (web page); "greater than 2 MW" (request form)
rules.contract_term: no fixed term: the Electric Service Agreement remains in effect until terminated
rules.collateral: an irrevocable standby letter of credit kept for the whole term of service, amount set by the Cooperative (it may set minimums per MW or per MVA); 100 percent of the estimated construction cost (CIAC) paid within 10 business days of the Construction Development Agreement; a study deposit of $5,000 per MW of requested load, capped at $1,000,000
rules.exit_fee: no fixed fee: on termination all outstanding amounts fall due at once, and the member bears stranded transmission or distribution investment, underused or abandoned facilities, load below planned levels, decommissioning and any other unrecovered cost of serving it

queue_totals.figure: Letters of Agreement executed for approximately 49 GW of incremental load by 2031, including prospective load seeking Batch Zero; financial security received in July 2026 for 45 GW of prospective load seeking Batch Zero participation through 2032 (Q3 2026 10-Q, filed 28 October 2026)

795 requests in Oncor's active transmission LC&I interconnection queue at the end of the third quarter of 2026 (30 September 2026): approximately 293 GW from data centers and approximately 19 GW from other industrial sectors, including 4 GW of crypto-mining; Batch Zero (conditional ERCOT classification): approximately 24 GW base load, including 10 GW already energized, and 21 GW studied load where Oncor is the TSP
